Predict form of a LMM fitted with mmes

predict_mmes.Rd

predict method for class "mmes".

Usage

# S3 method for mmes
predict(object, Dtable=NULL, D, levels=NULL, sed=FALSE,
        pairwise=FALSE, adjust="none", df=Inf, PEV=TRUE, VarU=TRUE,
        observed=FALSE, maxMemoryMB=NULL, ...)

Arguments

object

a mixed model of class "mmes"

Dtable

a table specifying the terms to be included or averaged.

An "include" term uses the cells matching each prediction row. For categorical random effects these are mapped within the fitted term, including fitted cells without records. Numeric fixed terms retain their evaluated covariate values rather than being replaced by indicators.

An "include and average" term means that the included cells of that effect are averaged: each prediction row is divided by the number of cells of the term present with it (for fixed terms this count includes the reference cells absorbed in the intercept).

An "average" term alone averages over the selected factor levels. For categorical terms the weights are 1/#levels; numeric fixed terms are evaluated at their covariate settings before averaging.

If a term is not considered "include" or "average" is then totally ignored in the BLUP and SE calculation.

The default rule to invoke when the user doesn't provide the Dtable is to include and average all terms that match the argument D.

Dtable contains only term-level rules, not level selections or numeric settings. Supply these through the levels argument; resolved settings are returned separately as levels. A levels column in a supplied Dtable is rejected; move its non-NULL entries to the named levels argument.

With observed=TRUE, start from object$Dtable and change the random-term flags. Fixed flags must remain unchanged: all fixed terms use empirical retained-record averages. For random terms, include=TRUE alone uses the empirical within-group average of the fitted random design. With an indicator design, include=TRUE, average=TRUE instead gives equal weight to selected coefficient levels that co-occur with each prediction group. A group with no such levels is an error. include=FALSE, average=TRUE gives equal weight to all selected fitted coefficient levels, even if not observed within a prediction group. Both flags FALSE exclude the term. Random-level restrictions may be supplied through the levels argument. These observed-path weights do not construct a Cartesian grid.

D

a character string specifying the variable used to extract levels for the rows of the D matrix and its construction. Alternatively, the D matrix (of class dgCMatrix) specifying the matrix to be used for the predictions directly.

levels

an optional named list whose names are values of Dtable$term. Selections and resolved numeric settings are returned separately as levels, and can be reused alongside the returned Dtable. NULL entries mean unrestricted factor levels or default numeric settings. Levels are written as data levels for fixed factors ("a:b" for interactions, e.g. "Victory:0.2"), as cell labels for categorical random terms (e.g. "CA.2011:genotype1" for an Env by Name term), and as numeric settings for covariate terms. A term containing one numeric variable accepts a numeric scalar, e.g. levels=list("Env:cov"=5). Numeric or mixed terms also accept a named per-variable list, e.g. levels=list("Env:cov"=list(Env=c("CA.2011", "CA.2012"), cov=5)). Each numeric setting must be one finite value. Use the exact term spelling in object$Dtable$term. For an included categorical term matching the classify variable(s) the levels select the prediction rows, in the given order, and may include levels without records (e.g. levels only present in Gu). For other included or averaged terms, only the listed levels enter the inclusion or the average. Restrictions are term-specific: selecting levels of V does not automatically restrict V:N.

sed

if TRUE, return the matrix of standard errors of differences sed and its summary avsed (mean, minimum and maximum).

pairwise

TRUE for all pairwise differences between predictions, or a single prediction level to compare every other prediction against it.

adjust

multiplicity adjustment passed to p.adjust.

df

degrees of freedom for pairwise tests: Inf (normal-based, default), a positive number, "residual" for n - rank(X), or "satterthwaite"/"kr" (see wald_mmes). The latter two apply to differences involving only fixed effects; differences involving random effects keep normal-based tests (df=Inf). With "kr" the SED of those differences uses the Kenward-Roger adjusted covariance.

PEV

Logical, default TRUE. Return the full target prediction-error covariance as PEV and its diagonal as pvals$pev. When FALSE, only these additional outputs are omitted; vcov and std.error remain available for compatibility.

VarU

Logical, default TRUE. Return the sampling covariance of the random contribution as VarU, its diagonal as pvals$var.u, and the sampling covariance of the entire predictor as sampling.vcov. Set FALSE to skip the additional relationship solves and outputs. These calculations require a Gaussian Henderson or direct fit. For PQL predictions use VarU=FALSE; their existing working-model uncertainty remains an approximation.

observed

Logical, default FALSE. For rank-reduced Henderson or direct fits, character classify predictions stop before expanding a Cartesian grid by default. Opt in with observed=TRUE to predict the observation-weighted fixed predictor within each observed categorical combination of D in the retained fitting data. All fixed terms contribute their empirical within-group averages; random contributions are excluded by default but can be explicitly included or averaged using random rows of Dtable. This is not a balanced-grid marginal mean. Only categorical classify variables in the fixed formula are supported. levels may contain an entry named exactly as D, with unique observed labels to select and order rows, and entries named by fitted random terms to restrict their coefficients. Random labels may be coefficient names, main-effect levels, covariance coordinate levels, or structured cell labels such as "north:b3". Unobserved requested combinations are errors, not silently removed. Explicit matrix contrasts must use observed=FALSE and are still checked for estimability. This option is not used for full-rank fits.

maxMemoryMB

Positive finite workspace budget in decimal MB for rank-reduced and direct-engine predictions. Defaults to the fitted control$execution$denseMemoryMB, or 1000 MB for older objects. Before grouped design construction or covariance solves, an estimate includes dense engine-coordinate right-hand sides, solve copies, covariance outputs, and requested SED/pairwise workspace. It is an allocation safeguard, not a bound on total process memory or sparse factorization fill-in. Exceeding the budget raises an error suggesting fewer levels or smaller explicit contrast batches. PEV=FALSE does not eliminate the mandatory full vcov. Increase the budget only when memory is available. Direct predictions additionally check observation-space factorization, relationship covariance and contrast workspace against this budget.

...

Further arguments to be passed.

Details

Direct Gaussian and direct PQL fits support the same classify, explicit contrast, Dtable, level-selection, SED and pairwise workflows as Henderson fits. They retain sparse prepared designs and final covariance inputs when output$coefficientMatrix=TRUE (default), and compute contrast error covariance in observation space without forming Henderson equations or requiring postPEV() first. Gaussian uncertainty is conditional on fitted covariance parameters; PQL uncertainty is additionally a working-model approximation on the link scale. For PQL set VarU=FALSE. Coefficient predictions are \(L_b\hat\beta+L_u\hat u\); formula offsets are not added automatically. These are not future-response prediction intervals. Older direct fits lacking retained covariance inputs must be refitted.

This function allows to produce predictions specifying those variables that define the margins of the hypertable to be predicted (argument D). Predictions are obtained for each combination of values of the specified variables that is present in the data set used to fit the model. See vignettes for more details.

For a rank-reduced fit, predict(fit, D="locale:cultivar", observed=TRUE) constructs sparse averages directly from retained observed combinations, without generating the locale-by-cultivar Cartesian product. Returned rows are ordered by first appearance unless levels specifies their order. Missing-response rows excluded from the fit cannot create prediction rows. An observed marginal prediction, such as D="locale", averages the fitted fixed predictor using the observed records in each locale; it is not an equally weighted or cultivar-adjusted comparison. Estimability is checked before covariance computation. Manual random contributions are added in the same public coefficient coordinates as explicit contrasts, so their prediction-error, sampling covariance and pairwise calculations follow the fitted engine's usual path. When include=TRUE alone has random-level restrictions, omitted coefficient contributions are zeroed without renormalizing the empirical group weights. Use include=TRUE, average=TRUE for equally weighted selected co-occurring indicator levels.

For categorical structured random terms, the fitted covariance-coordinate and main-effect levels define the genetic prediction weights, even when a cell has no observations. The levels argument can additionally request fitted levels present only in Gu. Unsupported random designs that cannot be mapped for all prediction rows produce a warning; an explicit D matrix can be used for these designs.

Numeric fixed terms, including factor-by-covariate interactions, are evaluated using the fitted fixed formula and contrasts. Unless overridden, each numeric variable is set to its mean in the retained fitting data. Factor levels are equally weighted when averaged. Thus an averaged Env:cov term with one slope per environment uses mean(cov)/nlevels(Env) for each slope, not 1/nlevels(Env).

Write \(D=[L_b,L_u]\). The target is \(t=L_b\beta+L_u u\) and its predictor is \(\hat t=L_b\hat\beta+L_u\hat u\). The existing prediction PEV and VarU matrices are for the linear combinations represented by the final returned D, after applying Dtable and levels, not copies of model-level effect variances. Each covariance matrix has one row and column per requested prediction. The existing vcov, optional PEV, and squared std.error refer to \(\operatorname{Var}(t-\hat t)\), not generally to \(\operatorname{Var}(\hat t)\). They are computed from $$\operatorname{Var}(t-\hat t)=D C_0^{-1}D',$$ where \(C_0\) is the original-scale Henderson coefficient matrix defined in postVarU. For Henderson fits, the stored system C is solved against contrast transposes and the result multiplied by Cscale. Arbitrary contrasts work regardless of computeCi; no stored Ci is used. Direct fits obtain the equivalent joint error covariance blocks in observation space, as described in postPEV; they also support singular random-effect covariance, for which \(G^{-1}\) need not exist.

With \(Q=(C_0^{-1})_{uu}\) and \(B=(C_0^{-1})_{bb}\), the new outputs are $$\mathrm{VarU}=L_u(G-Q)L_u',$$ $$\mathrm{sampling.vcov}=L_b B L_b'+L_u(G-Q)L_u'.$$ The BLUE and BLUP have zero sampling cross-covariance, whereas the fixed/random blocks of the inverse Henderson matrix describe error covariance and generally are not zero. In particular, subtracting the full target PEV from \(L_uGL_u'\) is incorrect if fixed effects are included. A fixed-only prediction has zero VarU, but generally nonzero sampling.vcov and PEV. Random-only predictions satisfy \(L_uGL_u'=\mathrm{PEV}+\mathrm{VarU}\).

The implementation evaluates full, random-only and fixed-only contrasts using one operation-local factorization in the selected formulation. Prior products use the term structure \(G_k=\Sigma_k\otimes A_k\) and sparse relationship-precision solves. Henderson does not construct the observation covariance \(V\) or its inverse; direct fits factor \(V\) and use termwise relationship products. Additional matrices require quadratic storage in the number of predictions. Rotation and factor-score mappings operate in public effect coordinates. New fits retain relationship precisions; older ordinary fits attempt model input reconstruction as described in postVarU.

All covariance outputs use the fitted variance components as fixed, omitting their estimation uncertainty. They are exact for known components and plug-in approximations for estimated components, for both ML and REML. SEDs, pairwise tests and std.error retain their PEV-based meaning; enabling VarU does not change those calculations. Direct and matrix-free solveOnly fits lack the stored coefficient system required here.

Categorical familym predictions return a trait-named list of scalar vectors and labelled categorical probability matrices; link predictions return ordinal/scalar vectors and nominal logit matrices. Row order is preserved within each trait, and traits absent from new data have empty outputs. Conditional prediction retains explicit shared or .familyCoordinate-specific random effects. se.fit=TRUE returns matching fit and se.fit lists. cov.fit=TRUE adds their joint flattened covariance, labelled by trait, category and within-trait row. Conditional uncertainty includes estimated ordinal cutpoints while holding covariance/shape coordinates fixed; uncertainty="full" includes all estimated parameters and mode dependence. All uncertainty is post-fit and memory-budgeted. Population prediction integrates the fitted structured latent covariance, including supplied relationship precision and arbitrary design loadings. Population standard errors propagate all estimated outer parameters and report uncertainty="full". Classify aggregation remains unsupported.

Native Laplace fits accept newdata, type, re.form, se.fit, and cov.fit through .... Random-effect and observation-space Laplace backends retain the same prediction and uncertainty targets. Observation fits reconstruct operation-local mode and fixed-effect Schur solves rather than a random-effect Hessian. For conditional predictions at known random-effect levels or zero-random-effect predictions, se.fit=TRUE returns a list with fit, se.fit, and cov.fit=NULL. The standard errors use the joint fixed/random conditional observed-information inverse, with fitted covariance and family parameters held fixed. Response-scale standard errors use the delta method. Setting cov.fit=TRUE additionally returns the complete link-scale or response-scale prediction covariance and requires se.fit=TRUE. Solve panels are controlled by output$panelSize, and full covariance workspace is checked against execution$denseMemoryMB. Population-mean uncertainty is propagated through fixed-effect and covariance-parameter and family-parameter curvature for supported structured random effects. This is uncertainty in an integrated mean, not a future-response interval. Aggregation is not implemented. With a nontrivial zipoisson(zero=~covariates) formula, prediction uncertainty instead propagates the joint outer-parameter covariance, including zero coefficients and cross-covariances. Conditional predictions also propagate conditional-mode dependence and local latent covariance. All these calculations occur after fitting; they are local approximations, not future-response prediction intervals. Zero-formula factor coding, transformations and offsets are evaluated from the training basis.

Single-family ordinal Laplace fits default to type="response" (or "probabilities"): a labelled observation-by-category probability matrix. type="link" returns the latent predictor and type="mean" the expected numeric category code. The fitted factor basis, column selection and offsets are reused for new data. Conditional predictions require known random levels; re.form=NA sets random effects to zero. re.form="population" integrates category probabilities with exact normal convolution for probit and 24-node Gaussian quadrature for logit, under the same structured latent covariance as other Laplace population predictions. Ordinal uncertainty propagates the full outer-parameter covariance, including cutpoint cross-covariances and conditional-mode dependence; conditional predictions additionally include local random-mode variance. Probability se.fit has the same labelled matrix shape as fit. Probability cov.fit uses column-major order (all prediction rows for category one, then category two, etc.), with labels category:row. These are post-fit local approximations, not calibrated response intervals.

Single-family multinomial fits return labelled category probabilities by default; type="link" returns the \(K-1\) reference-category logits. Conditional prediction requires known random levels, while re.form=NA sets random effects to zero. re.form="population" averages category probabilities over the fitted Gaussian latent distribution, rather than setting random effects to zero or averaging logits. It supports up to four response categories, structured temporal/spatial effects, random slopes and supplied relationship precision, and sums covariance contributions from independent terms. Each observation uses its actual joint logit covariance. New independent group levels are allowed provided the fixed-effect design is supported and the relationship precision is identity. New time/site coordinates or unknown relationship levels are rejected: the coordinate basis must be represented when fitting. Conditional prediction can borrow information for represented latent coordinates without an observed response; it does not extrapolate to an undefined covariance basis. Integration uses deterministic tensor normal quadrature on the nonzero logit-covariance eigenspace: 24- and 32-point rules must agree to within \(10^{-6}\) absolute probability in every cell. The returned 32-point result is a numerical approximation; rule agreement is not a guaranteed error bound. Estimated workspace is guarded by execution$denseMemoryMB. Population type="link" is rejected. Population se.fit and cov.fit propagate all estimated outer parameters after fitting and report uncertainty="full"; covariance uses category-major order and labels category:row. Classify-table aggregation remains unsupported. se.fit=TRUE returns probability standard errors by the delta method; conditional uncertainty uses the joint fixed/random conditional curvature with fitted covariance parameters held fixed. These calculations happen after fitting; they are not calibrated prediction intervals. Nominal models additionally accept uncertainty="conditional" (the unchanged default) or uncertainty="full" through .... The latter requires se.fit=TRUE and uses the full marginal Laplace parameter covariance, including free random-covariance coordinates. Conditional prediction differentiates the fitted random modes as parameters change and adds random-mode posterior covariance; re.form=NA instead uses the marginal fixed-coefficient covariance with zero random effects. Response-scale covariance uses the softmax delta method. This is a first-order post-fit approximation, not a bootstrap, simultaneous confidence region, or future-response prediction interval. It requires valid parameter curvature and respects the dense-memory budget; all calculations are opt-in and neither change fitting nor its stored object.

Value

pvals

the table of predictions according to the specified arguments.

vcov

The full target prediction-error covariance, always returned.

PEV

When requested, identical to vcov; its diagonal is pvals$pev.

VarU

When requested, sampling covariance of the predicted random contribution only; its diagonal is pvals$var.u.

sampling.vcov

When VarU=TRUE, sampling covariance of the entire fixed-plus-random predictor. This is not the covariance used for standard errors.

D

the model matrix for predictions as defined in Welham et al.(2004).

Dtable

the compact table specifying the terms to include and terms to be averaged.

levels

the named list of level selections and resolved numeric settings used to construct D. Numeric defaults on the regular prediction path are retained-data means. With observed=TRUE, fixed numeric contributions remain empirical within-group averages; numeric overrides require explicit estimable contrasts.

observed

For observed=TRUE, a list containing the classify values, retained observation counts per prediction, and a description of the empirical weighting and selected random terms. The returned Dtable records the resolved random flags; levels stores level restrictions separately.

sed, avsed

when sed=TRUE: the standard errors of differences, sqrt(v_ii + v_jj - 2 v_ij) from vcov, and their mean, minimum and maximum.

pairwise

when requested: a data frame with level1, level2, difference (level1 - level2), SED, statistic, df, p.value and p.adjusted.

References

Welham, S., Cullis, B., Gogel, B., Gilmour, A., and Thompson, R. (2004). Prediction in linear mixed models. Australian and New Zealand Journal of Statistics, 46, 325 - 347.

Author

Giovanny Covarrubias-Pazaran

Examples


data(DT_yatesoats, package="enhancer")
DT <- DT_yatesoats
m3 <- mmes(fixed=Y ~ V + N + V:N ,
           random = ~ B + B:MP,
           rcov=~units,
           data = DT)

m3 <- postPEV(m3, mode = 2)
 
#############################
## predict means for nitrogen
#############################
Dt <- m3$Dtable; Dt
# first fixed effect just average
Dt[1,"average"] = TRUE
# second fixed effect include
Dt[2,"include"] = TRUE
# third fixed effect include and average
Dt[3,"include"] = TRUE
Dt[3,"average"] = TRUE
Dt

pp=predict(object=m3, Dtable=Dt, D="N")
pp$pvals

#############################
## predict means for variety
#############################

Dt <- m3$Dtable; Dt
# first fixed effect include
Dt[1,"include"] = TRUE
# second fixed effect just average
Dt[2,"average"] = TRUE
# third fixed effect include and average
Dt[3,"include"] = TRUE
Dt[3,"average"] = TRUE
Dt

pp=predict(object=m3, Dtable=Dt, D="V")
pp$pvals

#############################
## predict means for nitrogen:variety
#############################
# prediction matrix D based on (equivalent to classify in asreml)
Dt <- m3$Dtable; Dt
# first fixed effect include and average
Dt[1,"include"] = TRUE
Dt[1,"average"] = TRUE
# second fixed effect include and average
Dt[2,"include"] = TRUE
Dt[2,"average"] = TRUE
# third fixed effect include and average
Dt[3,"include"] = TRUE
Dt[3,"average"] = TRUE
Dt

pp=predict(object=m3, Dtable=Dt, D="N:V")
pp$pvals

#############################
## select levels through the argument, keeping Dtable compact
#############################
Dt <- m3$Dtable
Dt$average[Dt$term %in% c("1", "V", "V:N")] <- TRUE
Dt$include[Dt$term %in% c("N", "V:N")] <- TRUE

p <- predict(m3, D="N", Dtable=Dt,
             levels=list(N=c("0.6", "0.2")))
p$pvals
p$levels[["N"]]

p2 <- predict(m3, D="N", Dtable=p$Dtable, levels=p$levels)
all.equal(p$D, p2$D)

## Covariances of the requested linear combinations
p <- predict(m3, D="N", Dtable=Dt, PEV=TRUE, VarU=TRUE)
p$PEV
p$VarU
p$sampling.vcov
randomColumns <- seq.int(nrow(m3$b)+1L, nrow(m3$bu))
randomD <- p$D[,randomColumns,drop=FALSE]
full <- postVarU(m3, mode=2)
all.equal(unname(p$VarU),
          unname(as.matrix(randomD %*% full$VarU %*% t(randomD))))
